projectAbout:
Food delivery for one city. Customers order in the app or on the website, restaurants cook, couriers deliver.

Start with **Ordering**, which every order passes through. **Delivery** covers courier matching and tracking.

objects.name: Customer
objects.description: Orders from the Plum app or the website.

objects.name: Restaurant
objects.description: Kitchen staff. Accept orders and mark them ready.

objects.name: Courier
objects.description: Carries the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.

objects.name: Support agent
objects.description: Answers customer and courier tickets.

objects.name: Ordering
objects.description:
Everything customer-facing: menus, basket, payment.

The **Order API** is the only entry point. It stores orders in Postgres and publishes each
new order to **Order events**, which **Delivery** consumes.

objects.name: Delivery
objects.description:
Assigns a courier to each order and tracks it to the door.

Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking feeds the customer's map.

objects.name: Notifications
objects.description: Push, SMS and email. The only system that talks to a messaging provider.

objects.name: Back office
objects.description: Internal tools for Plum staff. Not exposed to customers or couriers.

objects.name: Stripe
objects.description: Card payments and refunds. Plum never handles card numbers.

objects.name: Twilio
objects.description: SMS delivery.

objects.name: Mapbox
objects.description: Maps, geocoding and travel times.

objects.name: Customer app
objects.description:
Mobile client. Browse, order, pay, follow the courier.

Stores only the basket and the session.

objects.name: Website
objects.description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are server-rendered so search engines can index them.

objects.name: Kitchen tablet
objects.description: Alerts on a new order. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** for pickup.

objects.name: Order API
objects.description:
Entry point for every client, and the only service that touches the **Orders DB**.

- `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
- `POST /orders` places an order
- `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one

objects.name: Orders DB
objects.description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.

objects.name: Menu cache
objects.description: Menus, 5 min TTL. A restaurant's edit appears when the entry expires.

data.name: Keys

shown.name: Keys

objects.name: Order events
objects.description:
One message per order change: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

Dispatch and the warehouse are consumers.

data.name: order-events
data.note: Keyed by order id, so each order's messages stay ordered.

shown.name: order-events
shown.note: Keyed by order id, so each order's messages stay ordered.

objects.name: Menu
objects.description: Serves menus from the cache, and from the database on a miss.

objects.name: Basket
objects.description: Holds the picked items and asks **Pricing** for the running total.

objects.name: Pricing
objects.description:
Computes the total: items, delivery fee and any promotion.

The fee is based on Mapbox travel distance, rounded up to the next 500 m.

A meal deal is priced by pricing each of its parts, and a part can be a deal too.

snippets.title: Delivery fee

objects.name: Checkout
objects.description:
Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

The card is charged only when the restaurant accepts. A rejection releases the hold.

objects.name: Order status
objects.description: Advances an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, publishing each step.

snippets.title: Accepting an order
snippets.text:
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'

objects.name: Refunds
objects.description: Refunds the card, then marks the order refunded. Full or per line.

objects.name: Courier app
objects.description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Reports position every 5 s while a job is open.

objects.name: Dispatch
objects.description:
Assigns a courier to each new order.

Consumes `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.

objects.name: Live tracking
objects.description: Relays courier position to the customer's map. Positions older than 1 min are dropped.

objects.name: Fleet DB
objects.description: Couriers, vehicles and last known position.

objects.name: Matcher
objects.description: Ranks idle couriers near a restaurant by estimated arrival.

objects.name: ETA
objects.description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and vehicle.

objects.name: Offers
objects.description:
Offers the job to one courier at a time with a 30 s timeout.

A refusal or timeout moves to the next courier.

objects.name: Notifier
objects.description: Chooses push, SMS or email per message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.

objects.name: Message templates
objects.description: Message text, per language.

objects.name: Admin dashboard
objects.description: Restaurants, delivery zones, promotions and the weekly reports.

objects.name: Support console
objects.description: Look up an order, see where the courier is, issue a refund.

objects.name: Data warehouse
objects.description: Every order event, kept for reporting. Only the **Admin dashboard** reads it.

steps.text: Reports that the charge went through
Publishes the paid event and carries on without waiting
Dispatch consumes it and starts looking for a courier
Streams the same event to the warehouse
steps.ends: Order events → Data warehouse in Back office

steps.text: The kitchen taps Accept
Sends the acceptance
Captures the amount it held
Times out after 5 s and retries
Confirms the charge
Marks the order paid
Declines the card
steps.description: A decline is not retried. The hold is released and the app asks for another card.

steps.text: Asks for another card
Shows that the card was declined

charge.text: Waits 1 s, then 2 s, then 4 s between tries. Plum's client gives up after three.

steps.text: Rides into streets with a weak signal
About a third of the pings are lost on the way
steps.description:
On a weak signal, pings never reach **Live tracking**. The app does not retry them, since a
newer one follows in 5 s.

steps.text: Sends the positions that did arrive
steps.ends: Live tracking → Customer app in Ordering

steps.text: The courier jumps across the map
Keeps the last position it got
steps.description:
Nothing is written for a lost ping, so the courier can look parked for 10 s or more to readers
of **Fleet DB**, such as the matcher ranking couriers for the next offer.

steps.text: Places an order
The placed order reaches Dispatch
Finds idle couriers near the restaurant
Asks Mapbox how far each courier is
steps.description:
**ETA** asks for each courier's travel time (distance, traffic, vehicle), and the **Matcher**
ranks them by arrival. The quickest gets the first offer.

steps.text: Sends the offer as a push
Accepts within 30 seconds
Hands the food over at the counter
Streams its position every 5 seconds
steps.description:
Only while a job is open. Positions older than 1 min are dropped, so a courier who loses
signal freezes on the map until a fresh position arrives.

steps.text: The customer's map follows the courier
steps.ends: Live tracking → Customer app in Ordering

steps.text: Hands the food over at the door
Marks the order delivered
steps.ends: Courier app → Order API in Ordering

steps.text: Places an order in the dinner rush
The placed event waits behind the dinner rush
steps.description: A single consumer reads every `placed` event. When orders arrive faster than it reads, they queue.

steps.text: Finds couriers minutes after the customer paid
Opens the order to see where the food is
Opens the live map

steps.text: Sends its position
Stores it

steps.ends: Live tracking → Customer app in Ordering

steps.text: Marks the order delivered
steps.ends: Courier app → Order API in Ordering

steps.text: Closes the live map

steps.text: Taps Place order on the hotel wifi
POST /orders reaches a sign-in page instead
steps.description: Hotel wifi holds every request until the guest signs in, so the call never reaches the **Order API**.

steps.text: Waits for a reply and offers a Retry button

The placed order reaches the Matcher
Asks who is quickest
Asks Mapbox for travel times and is turned away

steps.text: Falls back to straight-line distance and ranks more roughly
Opens a restaurant
Asks for a restaurant's menu
Looks the menu up
Returns the cached menu

Caches it for 5 min
Returns the menu
Shows the dishes and prices
Places an order
The placed order reaches Dispatch
Offers the job; the nearest courier doesn't answer in 30 s

A courier taps Accept
The offers stop

Rings the restaurant's tablet and gets no answer
steps.description: The tablet lost its Wi-Fi or ran out of battery, so nobody sees the order. The kitchen has two minutes.

flows.name: A double tap sends the order twice

steps.text: Taps Place order, and again when nothing seems to happen
The same order arrives twice
steps.description: The app resends when the first reply is slow. Both copies carry the same idempotency key.

steps.text: Saves the first copy and refuses the second
Taps Place order
POST /orders with the basket
A write gets no answer, because the primary has failed
Asks the customer to try again in a minute
A standby takes over as the primary
steps.description: The standby has to catch up and be promoted. Plum rehearses this quarterly. Promotion has taken under a minute so far.

steps.text: The next write goes through
Fills a basket and taps Place order
POST /orders with the basket
steps.description: The app sends an idempotency key, so a double tap or a retry places one order.

steps.text: Holds the amount on the card
steps.description:
**Checkout** asks Stripe to authorise the total. The charge happens on acceptance; a refusal
releases the hold.

steps.text: Saves the order as placed
Publishes the order
Dispatch starts looking for a courier
The restaurant's tablet rings
steps.description:
The kitchen has two minutes to accept. Then the order is cancelled, the hold released and
the customer notified.

steps.text: Asks for the total of a basket that holds a meal deal
Prices a deal by pricing each of its parts, down to plain items that have a price
steps.description:
A plain item has a price, and that is where it stops. A deal holds items and other deals, so
Pricing asks itself about each part and adds up what comes back.

The menu editor allows deals inside deals three deep at most. The picture shows three levels
because that is the limit.

steps.text: Hands back the total
Asks for a refund in the support console

steps.text: Sends the refund to the Order API
steps.ends: Support console in Back office → Refunds in Order API

steps.text: Stripe has refunded the charge
steps.description: The money is already back on the card. What can still go wrong is Plum's own records.

steps.text: Can't mark the order refunded, because Orders DB doesn't answer
steps.ends: Refunds in Order API → Orders DB

steps.text: Leaves the order marked paid, though the money is back
Still sends the customer a refund confirmation
steps.ends: Refunds in Order API → Notifier in Notifications

steps.text: Finds the order in the support console
Asks for a refund, in full or by line
The money goes back to the card
steps.description:
Stripe refunds the original charge. The order is marked refunded only after Stripe confirms,
so the database never records a refund that didn't happen.

steps.text: Requests a confirmation
Hands the SMS to Twilio
The customer reads that the money is back

compare.note:
The same refund twice. Right: what support sees, from the console to the customer's SMS. Left: the refund inside Ordering when Orders DB doesn't answer. Stripe returns the money, the order stays marked paid, and the customer still gets a confirmation.

Support, Back office and Stripe are in both flows.

steps.text: The kitchen taps Accept
Sends the acceptance
Marks the order accepted
Captures the amount it held
steps.description: The card is charged here for the first time. The capture is its own flow because the bank can be slow.

steps.text: Publishes accepted
Asks for a push to the customer
Pushes the news to the customer's phone
Shows that the kitchen has started
Places an order
Asks for an SMS that confirms it
Hands the confirmation to Twilio
The carrier drops it before it reaches the phone

The hold is slow while Stripe shuts down
The hold times out

steps.text: Offers pay at the door
steps.ends: Checkout in Order API → Customer app

steps.text: Picks pay at the door
The status page says Stripe is restarting
The next check finds it coming back up
The hold goes through
Calls Plum's webhook: the charge went through
steps.description: Stripe initiates this call, not Plum. The order is marked paid when it arrives.

failures.name: Plum fail scenario
failures.about: Rated by the ordering team from a year of incidents and support tickets.

severity.high: A customer loses money or the kitchen stops

detection.low: An alert fires within a minute

modes.effect: The order waits on a hold that may or may not exist.
modes.cause: Stripe is slow, or the network between Plum and Stripe drops.
modes.controls: Three tries with backoff. The idempotency key stops a double hold.
modes.action: Page when over 1% of holds time out for 5 min.

modes.effect: The order is not placed, and the customer is asked for another card.
modes.cause: The card is short of funds, expired or blocked.
modes.controls: The hold is released and the app asks again.

modes.mode: Stripe refunds the money but the database write fails
modes.effect: The customer has the money back, and Plum still shows the order as paid.
modes.cause: Orders DB is unreachable when the refund is saved.
modes.controls: Support can see the refund in Stripe.
modes.action: Compare refunds with Stripe every night.
modes.description:
The refund and the write are separate steps, so one can succeed without the other.
The nightly comparison finds the gap but does not close it.

modes.effect: No order can be placed or read until it is back.
modes.cause: The primary fails, or a failover takes longer than planned.
modes.controls: A standby takes over within a minute.

modes.mode: A double tap places two orders
modes.effect: The customer is charged twice for one basket.
modes.cause: The app resends when the first reply is slow.
modes.controls: Every order carries an idempotency key. A repeated key is refused.

modes.mode: Serves a menu up to 5 min old
modes.effect: A customer orders a dish the kitchen has just taken off.
modes.controls: The kitchen can refuse an item, and the customer is told.

modes.mode: Mapbox calls fail at dinner rush
modes.effect: Dispatch has no travel times, so couriers are matched on distance alone.
modes.cause: Plum exceeds Mapbox's rate limit above 900 orders a minute.
modes.controls: Dispatch falls back to straight-line distance.
modes.action: Batch the travel-time calls, as the second run tries.

modes.effect: Live tracking shows an old position, or none.

modes.mode: Dispatch reads events slower than they arrive
modes.effect: A courier is matched minutes after the customer paid, and the arrival time shown is wrong.
modes.cause: A burst of orders (the dinner rush) outruns Dispatch's single consumer.
modes.controls: A lag alert fires at 30 s.

modes.mode: The tablet goes offline and nobody accepts within two minutes
modes.effect: The customer waits two minutes, then is told the order was cancelled.
modes.cause: The tablet loses its Wi-Fi, or its battery runs out.
modes.controls: The order cancels itself and the card hold is released.

modes.effect: The order waits for a courier, and the arrival time shown keeps growing.
modes.cause: The couriers near the restaurant are busy, out of signal or away from their phones.
modes.controls: Each offer moves on to the next courier. When the list runs out, the customer is told.
modes.action: Widen the search when the list runs out.

modes.mode: The courier loses signal and the map freezes
modes.effect: The customer sees a courier who has stopped moving.
modes.cause: The courier drives through a tunnel or a dead zone.
modes.controls: Positions older than 1 min are dropped, so the map holds still until a fresh one arrives.

modes.mode: Twilio accepts an SMS and the carrier drops it
modes.effect: The customer never gets the confirmation or the courier's arrival message.
modes.cause: The number is wrong, switched off or blocked by the carrier.
modes.controls: None. Plum does not read Twilio's delivery receipts.
modes.action: Read the delivery receipts and alert when fewer than 95% arrive.

modes.effect: Reports run late. Orders carry on.
modes.cause: The cluster is being upgraded, or its disk is full.
modes.controls: Events stay on the stream and replay when it recovers.
